summary: This note surveys recent innovations in solar energy conversion and storage from 2023-2024, including a 40% efficient solar cell, a solid-state battery module, photonic crystals, aesthetic solar overlays, artificial photosynthesis, solar roadways, and a wind-solar hybrid system. It highlights efficiency gains, storage improvements, and new integration approaches that could reduce reliance on fossil fuels.
one_line: Overview of 2023-2024 solar breakthroughs spanning high-efficiency cells, solid-state storage, photonic crystals, solar skins, artificial photosynthesis, solar roadways, and wind-solar hybrids.
key_facts: On September 15, 2023, at the International Symposium on Green Energy in Berlin, Dr. Ava Richardson unveiled the 'Ultra-Absorbent Photonic Cell' developed with engineers at SolTech Innovations.
The Ultra-Absorbent Photonic Cell has a 40% efficiency rate, versus 15-20% for conventional solar cells, using a multi-junction structure that also captures the near-infrared band.
EnergyVault, co-founded by Jamal Greene and Priya Singh, introduced the 'EverCharge Battery Module' on November 24, 2023.
The EverCharge Battery Module is a lithium-ion alternative with a solid-state electrolyte, charges in nearly half the time of lithium-ion batteries, and degrades less than 1% per year.

On January 5, 2024, a team led by physicist Dr. Hector Navarro at the University of Solar Research in Nevada introduced a 'photonic crystal' that focuses and guides light waves to increase contact time with absorbing layers.
The photonic crystals can be retrofitted into existing solar panels and may reduce the silicon required in panels, lowering costs.
AesthetiSolar, with designers Chloe Zhao and Tariq Al-Hassan, made headlines around mid-2024 for 'Solar Skins,' customizable overlays that mimic roofing materials or patterns.
Solar Skins include a spectrum-shifting layer that funnels more energy to the solar cells beneath, enhancing efficiency.
On August 22, 2024, Dr. Lila Torres and her team at EcoSynth Labs published a paper on a synthetic leaf that converts water and carbon dioxide into oxygen and energy using sunlight.
The synthetic leaf uses a pair of advanced catalysts and an arrangement of light-absorbing dyes.
On March 10, 2024, SolPathways and the city of San Francisco announced the first-ever solar roadway using 'Solar Pave' technology.
Solar Pave combines ultra-durable glass panels with embedded photovoltaic cells, built-in LED road markings, and heating elements to stay ice-free in winter.
On September 9, 2024, TerraFusion launched 'Wind-Sun Synthesis,' combining wind turbines with wrap-around solar panels.
